findings.defect: The headline ("choosing the comparison is free, naming it is the whole problem") is already a paragraph of the paper, sitting fifteen lines above the route's own intended insertion point, and it is neither cited nor distinguished. The mathematical core is lem:alphabet-cover applied at the extreme letters; the rest is one line of arithmetic. Classified restatement.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.12176-12178, immediately after thm:top and immediately before def:bracket (the route asks to be inserted "after prop:bracket"): "Note the contrast with the threshold: by \Cref{lem:alphabet-cover} every letter in (0,1) is the midpoint of two others, so the largest of them is at least 1/2, and some vertex has value at least 1/2 unless every value is 0 or 1, which the attractor sweeps decide in linear time; the threshold plays no part in the difficulty, the naming of a vertex does." The three lines: (i) lem:alphabet-cover (l.2585) at lambda_max gives an AVERAGE vertex v of value lambda_max whose successors have distinct values straddling lambda_max; the larger exceeds every non-sink value, so it is t_1 (reduced), i.e. v in H u M; dually at lambda_min, L u M nonempty. (ii) w*(v)=(1+w*(u))/2>1/2 on H, =1/2 on M, <1/2 on L since w*>0 off the sinks. (iii) H nonempty -> pair (H, LuM); H empty, L nonempty -> (M,L); H=L=empty -> both extremes are 1/2, so 'all equal' is correct. I re-verified the statement independently on 525 reduced random stopping games (my /tmp/.../r18-audit-weakest-oracle-novelty/rnd.py, exact rationals): H>1/2, M=1/2, L<1/2, H u M and L u M nonempty, 'all equal' correct in all 293 flat cases, 0 failures. The mathematics is right; the novelty is not.

verdict:
VERDICT: blocked (downgraded from the route's "new-theorem").

1. DID THE OBJECT CHANGE? Half. The object is "fragments of the value order under polynomial-time reduction, coordinatised by scope and slack". The SCOPE coordinate is an object the paper already owns under another name: sec:selection is precisely a list of order fragments graded by what is named (thm:compare-equivalence, thm:order-determines, prop:no-halving, cor:wrong-equivalence, thm:top, thm:decide-one-bit, prop:bracket, rem:bsi, rem:alphabet-equivalence), and the paper even states the route's headline moral in prose at l.12176 ("the threshold plays no part in the difficulty, the naming of a vertex does"). The route adds one point to that list (choose-your-own-pair, which is free) and reproves two existing ones. The SLACK coordinate (Ord_eps / App_eps / Gap_eps) is genuinely new to the paper -- there is no approximation result anywhere in 229 pages -- but the two ends the route establishes are the trivial ones: standard complexity padding at the hard end, and lem:denominator-sharp in two lines at the easy end. The collapse of the scope axis into the paper's existing list was noticed, not proved.

2. QUALIFYING RESULT? Yes, barely: wo:eps-ladder(a)+(b) is a proved new-relation between objects the paper does not own (an eps-order oracle, an eps-approximation, a promise-threshold oracle) -- so the route is not automatically dead. But three of five results are restatements of lem:alphabet-cover, prop:no-halving(b) and prop:locality respectively, each derivable in three lines from the cited label; the round's rule 2 makes that a defect that costs the verdict, and round 17's failure mode (five of seven routes restating) repeats here. The one surviving new-relation is textbook binary search plus textbook padding, it terminates exactly at a known open question, and the route's fifth result is a one-hypothesis scope fix to an existing remark. Under rule 7 the route ends at statements of the same strength as the target (a tenth target-equivalent reformulation) and must say so; it does not.

3. CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? Not circular -- the reductions are honest and the constructions are real (I rebuilt FB5+/-, FB9+/- and ANYSET from the JSON with the independent harness: stopping, values as claimed, blocks identical, answers opposite). But two of the three "hard" results are new names for target-equivalences the paper has, and the "free" result is vacuous as a tool: by the route's own rem:wo-stalls the free datum separates no controlled vertex on H_m, WD, CC, S, S_2 or G_8, and it is contained in M1's preorder up to a strictness that comes from the sweeps the paper already runs. wo:free-blind's stated consequence is a one-liner from its own two neighbours and needs no witness family at all.

4. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it. The route proves nothing about prob:main that was not already available, and its only live direction, GAP 1, is the classical question whether SSG-Value reduces to its own inverse-polynomial-gap promise version; the route's barrier against it -- a black-box context on s vertices multiplies a gap by O(s) -- is rem:no-amplification, already in the paper, and rem:no-amplification already says black-box compositions are not the interesting class ("every transformation this document performs reads the input's edges and is outside their scope"). So the gap is: an amplifier, or a barrier, for edge-reading reductions -- the class in which thm:stopping-transform, thm:compare-equivalence, lem:normalform and thm:top all live -- and nothing here touches that class.

5. INTEGRATION. As submitted (500 lines of LaTeX, a new five-fragment definition block, a duplicated lem:alphabet-cover, a witness family redundant with prop:locality, and two renamed target-equivalences), integrating this makes the paper WORSE: more pages, a second copy of an existing lemma 9,000 lines from the first, and three theorem environments whose content is already numbered elsewhere. Compressed to about 25 lines it makes the paper slightly better. Worth integrating: (i) the admissibility-free form of rem:no-amplification -- two sentences inside that remark, replacing the misleading clause "what is excluded is a replay loop through calls and controlled vertices alone, which is not stopping" (the CONTEXT fails to be stopping there, the COMPOSITION need not), plus the biased GR(K) as the tight example (with the derivative corrected to 2i(K+1-i)/(K+1), i = ceil(K/2), and GR attributed to the paper's own l.2757); this is the route's one genuine correction. (ii) Two sentences appended to the l.12176 paragraph: the sink-adjacent average vertices split for free as H > M > L around 1/2 by lem:alphabet-cover at the extreme letters, so a strict pair is readable in one pass while every named-scope refinement is prop:no-halving(b) or thm:top -- cited to lem:alphabet-cover, not restated as a lemma. (iii) Optionally one short remark defining Ord_eps/App_eps/Gap_eps, recording their interreducibility, the padding end at 2^{-N^gamma}, and the pointer that the middle is the promise-gap question sec:composition cannot close. NOT worth integrating: lem:wo-extreme, def:wo-fragments as a display block, thm:wo-any-set as a theorem (one sentence under prop:no-halving), def:wo-fb and prop:wo-free-blind, cor:wo-context-blind, rem:wo-stalls (a measurement whose content is that the datum is useless), and thm:wo-eps-ladder(c).
